offset18.meaning: Raw offset18 initialization parameter of OffsetProgressiveCurve, an encoded 18-decimal fixed-point value compared against the report thresholds 1e9 and 1e18.
offset18.checkpoint: contract initialization (initialize), before the withdrawal attempt

user_has_deposit.meaning: The user holds an open deposit/position in the curve at the time the full withdrawal is attempted.

withdrawal_reverts.meaning: Execution outcome: the attempted full withdrawal deterministically reverts with PANIC(0x11) arithmetic underflow.
withdrawal_reverts.checkpoint: during/at the end of the full-withdrawal execution

assumptions: A full withdrawal of the user's entire open deposit is the attempted action (attempt_full_withdrawal).
Stored OFFSET is 0 before the withdrawal: divDown(OFFSET18, 1e18) truncates for OFFSET18 < 1e18 (offset_truncates_to_zero).
The withdrawal reaches the shares = squaredShares - inner conversion of OffsetProgressiveCurve, i.e. the affected arithmetic path executes.

unresolved.description: The report gives two different thresholds for the low-offset trigger: the title/impact say offset18 < 1e9 while the truncation mechanism requires OFFSET18 < 1e18; both are encoded exactly as stated.
It is not fully specified whether every full-withdrawal amount triggers the underflow or only particular amounts; the description suggests it applies generally.

limitations: funds_trapped (permanent blocking from fully closing the position) is a secondary consequence of the revert and is deferred; the core V uses the direct impact withdrawal_reverts_panic only.
No attacker or authorization claim is present: the affected caller is a user holding a deposit, so authorization-based patterns do not apply.
'Permanently blocked' is asserted without addressing alternative exits such as partial withdrawals or admin recovery.
Exact deposit balance, share quantity and withdrawal amount are unspecified, so the plan is kept symbolic.
